correctness.rationale: For an unglued radius-one planar sector and independent area-uniform sampling, the radial densities are 2r and the independent gap density is 2(theta-delta)/theta². Strict separate convexity of the squared distance in the two radii puts all maximizers at radial corners, with distances 1 for tip–arc pairs and 2 sin(theta/2) for the two ordered arc-endpoint pairs. They are disjoint types at theta=pi/3. Compactness localizes near-maximal configurations (also for moving angles after normalizing the angles by theta). In small fixed neighborhoods the positive linear loss bounds the local coordinates up to constants, so dominated convergence on bounded rescaled coordinates applies. At a tip–rim pair the loss is V+U cos(delta); the two orders together have density 8 epsilon³ U/theta² in rescaled radial and original angular variables. The radial simplex integral is 1/(6 cos²(delta)), and the double-angle secant-square integral equals -2 log cos(theta). The result is -8 log cos(theta)/(3 theta²), including at pi/3. At the rim endpoints the loss is s(U+V)+cT with s=sin(theta/2), c=cos(theta/2), and density 8 epsilon⁴ T/theta². The unit simplex T-moment after scaling is 1/24, giving 4/(3 theta² sin²(theta)). The normalized losses and slack have the two stated Dirichlet limits by their U and T density weights; the tip loss coordinate is U cos(delta) and the gap mark density is (theta-delta) sec²(delta)/[-log cos(theta)]. The rim orders are symmetric. For fixed lambda, the moving diameter raises the threshold relative to 1 by (sqrt(3) max(lambda,0)/2-1) epsilon plus O(epsilon²); the tip simplex weight has homogeneity three and its volume yields exactly the stated positive-part function. At lambda=2/sqrt(3) the threshold is 1-epsilon²/6+O(epsilon³), so the tip term is at most order epsilon⁶; for larger lambda there is no tip event for sufficiently small epsilon. In both cases the rim has a quartic contribution with coefficient 16/pi². The logarithmic derivatives/weighted secant-square identity establish the monotonicity assertions; more precisely the two-preimage range of the wide coefficient is strictly between its minimum and 16/pi², its excluded left-endpoint value. The exact polar survival disintegration follows by integrating the triangular angle law above the cosine-rule threshold. All limits used here are pointwise in the stated parameters. I inspected sector_verifier.py but did not execute it; its selected fixed-angle quadratures do not check the critical window or prove the limits, which are reproduced by the local integrals above.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The cone theorem already identifies the two radial contact types and the crossover at maximum unwrapped gap pi/3. Its exact integral can be mixed, but its leading asymptotics are pointwise in cone aperture. For a wide sector the cone mixture at a distance threshold near the planar diameter draws on a shrinking set of cone apertures, and in the critical window the aperture and loss both move. Termwise insertion of the pointwise equivalents does not justify either limit. The endpoint expansion with the new angular weight supplies the quartic constant, critical profile and conditional shape, rather than merely renaming an earlier coefficient. value.rationale: The sector is a standard line-picking domain, and the upper-endpoint law reveals something the diameter and moments alone miss: at the exact contact transition a continuum of tip–arc maximizers still dominates, whereas just above it a suppressed angular endpoint weight changes the exponent. The explicit critical profile resolves when that competition disappears at leading order, and the conditional shapes quantify the geometry of the rare pairs. These address a natural gap in the same-object distribution problem despite not giving a full CDF.
